posts.title: The freelance AV invoice: what to include
posts.description: What to put on an AV freelancer invoice: gig details, line items, overtime, expenses and payment terms, so AV companies pay without questions.
posts.imageAlt: The freelance AV invoice: what to include

faq.q: What should a freelance AV invoice include?
faq.a: Your name and contact details, the AV company and contact you're billing, an invoice number and date, the event, venue, show dates and your position, one line per charge with quantity and rate, the total, and your payment terms and payment method.

faq.q: Should I bill overtime on a separate line?
faq.a: Yes. Put overtime on its own line with the date and hours, and note on the day-rate line how many hours the day rate covers. That way the company can check it against the call times.

faq.q: Do I need to send a W-9 with my invoice?
faq.a: Most US companies ask independent contractors for a Form W-9 before paying them the first time. Sending it with your first invoice to a new company avoids a delay. Ask your accountant about your own tax situation.

faq.q: When should I send the invoice?
faq.a: As soon as the gig wraps, ideally within a day or two. Invoices sent while the show is fresh are easier for the company to match and approve.
